algorithm.closure_test: compiled context transitions remain inside the supported finite context set
algorithm.failure_policy: abstain globally when an exact conflict survives the declared memory budget
algorithm.novelty_boundary: suffix-memory growth is standard machinery; this experiment tests its explicit integration with predictive repair, dynamic closure, fail-closed verification, and infinite-fibre semantics
algorithm.repair: increase suffix order by one and rebuild from admitted observations
algorithm.standard_connections: variable-order Markov modelling, deterministic automata inference, predictive equivalence, causal-state ideas, and partition refinement
algorithm.verifier: same represented suffix must not have two distinct observed next symbols

conclusion.established_in_fixtures: observation-only counterexamples select a two-symbol history interface in the stable process; predictive repair alone gives two blocks, while dynamic closure forces the exact four-state machine
conclusion.failure_result: the same learner rejects every tested finite suffix budget on the countdown instead of fabricating a closed state
conclusion.next_falsifiable_experiment: replace exact conflicts by confidence-bounded distributional tests under controlled noise, while charging explicit memory and sampling costs
conclusion.not_established: robust stochastic learning, continuous observations, scalable active experiment selection, language acquisition, or superiority to trained neural sequence models

experiment.name: counterexample-guided observation-only interface learning
experiment.question: Can a learner with no hidden-state access discover the finite memory needed for prediction and autonomous continuation, and abstain when its finite memory budget cannot close the process?

negative_control.meaning: an exact learner must not silently turn irreconcilable observations into a deterministic autonomous law
negative_control.name: directly contradictory observation control

hidden_environment.access_policy: hidden states are used by the simulator and post-hoc evaluator only
